newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO detain alleged Moslem militants.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO detain alleged Moslem militants.

text.p: Israeli and Palestinian security forces on Thursday arrested alleged Moslem militants in separate raids following twin suicide attacks that killed 13 people in a market in Jewish west Jerusalem a day earlier.
All arrests but for one were in the West Bank.
In the Gaza Strip Palestinian self-rule enclave, PLO forces arrested Dr Abdel Aziz Rantisi, a Hamas political leader, his brother said.
"The intelligence forces arrested my brother," Salah Rantisi told Reuters on Thursday night.

A leaflet in the name of the Islamic Hamas group claimed responsibility for Wednesday's attacks. Hamas, opposed to PLO-Israel peace deals, has carried out bombings in Israel killing scores of people since the first accord in 1993.
Palestinian security officials had earlier said they arrested at least 10 Islamic Jihad and Hamas activists in PLO-ruled Bethlehem area.
Two weeks ago, Palestinian police found what they said was an explosives factory belonging to Hamas in an apartment at Beit Sahour village just outside Bethlehem.
The Palestinian security officials on Thursday said they made arrests in other areas under their control but refused to give details.
The Israeli army said its forces had arrested 28 Palestinians overnight in the West Bank in connection with "hostile terrorist activities". It gave no details.

At Dahariyeh village near the West Bank city of Hebron, Israeli forces detained nine members of two Palestinian families whose two sons, both Islamic militants, have been missing for 15 months, relatives said.
It was not immediately clear if the missing pair were the two suicide bombers who blew themselves up seconds apart in the market on Wednesday.
Israel's raids were carried out in Palestinian villages still under Israeli occupation.

In the Jenin area, in the north of the West Bank, soldiers arrested two activists belonging to Hamas, Palestinians said. As it happened, residents said Israel freed eight Islamic militants whose jail terms ended on Thursday.
In Qossin village near Nablus, the army arrested 15 Palestinians from one family early on Thursday but later released 10 of them, residents said.
In Anabta village, Israel arrested a 61-year-old man whose jailed son belongs to Hamas' military wing, Palestinians said.
Palestinian and Israeli security officials held three meetings late on Wednesday to discuss security matters following the bombings, PLO officials said.

They said all security and police offices throughout the West Bank and Gaza Strip were ordered to intensify patrols, set up checkposts and crack down on militants in line with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's declaration of a state of emergency in self-ruled areas on Wednesday.
Israel on Wednesday sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip and confined Palestinians to their cities and villages following the bombings.
